lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.43 - A Listen and number

details: Listen and number checks understanding of both time of day and activity vocabulary by having students number each image. Numbering supports sound–image association and strengthens recognition of key words.
Look for careful listening and accurate numbering of each image.
“I need some detective help today, class. Will you investigate with me? I have a series of picture clues, but I’m not sure what order to put them in.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.43 - B. Listen and choose

details: Listen and choose develops listening comprehension by having students compare what they hear with two or three visual options and identify the correct activity or time of day.
Look for careful listening, accurate selection of the correct picture from the options given, and consistent responses that match the audio.
“Hmm… these pictures are all different, but only one matches what we hear. Can you be picture detectives now and help me choose the right one? Let’s listen.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.99 - A Look and match

details: Look and match supports understanding of simple sentences by linking written descriptions of actions and locations to the correct images. This reinforces vocabulary recognition, and accurate interpretation of detail.
Look for correct matching of each sentence to the corresponding image, accurate recognition of action and location words, and confident completion of the task.
“Help, the sentences and pictures got muddled up! Can you help me match them together again? You can be matching detectives and use the pictures to help you.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.44 - C. Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops key listening and reading comprehension by helping students follow a short text about Mindy, Emily and her shopping list while hearing accurate pronunciation and reinforcing meaning through text support.
Look for careful listening, eyes tracking the text, and accurate following of key words such as juice, kitchen and milk.
“Now we need to be undercover detectives. Mindy and Emily are very busy in the kitchen. Let’s listen closely and follow along to see what’s on their shopping list.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.44 - D. Choose the correct answers 10m]

details: Choose the correct answers supports reading comprehension by having students identify key details from the text, such as where Emily is.
Look for correct choices that match the text, accurate understanding of location and item information, and neat bookwork.
“Oops, where are Mindy and Emily? What did they want to buy? Can you be story detectives and help me remember? Let’s look for clues in the story.”
